task: Degree-2 polynomial regression (PolynomialFeatures + LinearRegression) of crop yield on avg_temp, rainfall, pesticide usage; R2 on fitted data; deliver output.csv + output.txt

yield.csv.role: TARGET source (yield, hg/ha) + dimension keys country/crop_item/year
yield.csv.notes: FAO long format; Value is int64 hg/ha (no decimals); grain-only item list (10 crops); includes aggregate/historical areas (e.g. 'China, mainland', 'Ethiopia PDR', 'Belgium-Luxembourg').

pesticides.csv.notes: National totals (no crop_item breakdown) -> feature must be broadcast across crop items at merge time. Extremely right-skewed (median 1137 t vs max 1.8M t); consider keeping raw value (task spec) and being aware it dominates scale.

cleaning_required: strip BOM/leading space from first column name ('\ufeff Area' -> 'country'/'Area')
pd.to_numeric(..., errors='coerce') because column is object dtype with '..' placeholders (6 rows) plus 774 empty cells
avg_temp arrives as object with 2547 blanks -> coerce numeric and drop
country-year is NOT unique: ~2-3 records per country-year with slightly different values (two blended sources); must be aggregated (mean) or de-duplicated before a 1:1 merge
temp.csv.risk: Merging temp.csv as-is (without aggregation) turns the join into many-to-many and silently duplicates yield rows (13,130 clean country-year-item rows -> 28,242 rows). This is the single largest pipeline decision of the task.

join_design.join_keys: country(Area/country) + year(Year/year) for all four files; yield keeps crop_item

country_name_mismatch.notation: FAO long names in yield/pesticides/rainfall vs short names in temp.csv
country_name_mismatch.impact_of_exact_name_join: exact-name inner join keeps 13,130 complete rows / 101 countries; alias mapping adds ~2,035 rows / +13 countries but is an optional enrichment, not required by the task

join_design.overlap_window: all four sources overlap only in 1990-2013 (yield 1961-2016, pesticides 1990-2016, rainfall 1985-2017, temp 1743-2013)

data_quality_summary: temp.csv: 42,797 surplus duplicate country-year rows with conflicting values (must aggregate) - highest-impact issue
rainfall.csv: object dtype + '..' placeholders + BOM/space in first header -> numeric coercion and header normalization required
Country nomenclature differs between FAO files and temp.csv (temp uses short names) -> exact-name join loses ~50% of potential coverage
pesticides.csv is national-level: value repeats across the 10 crop items after merge (feature is not crop-specific)

yield.csv Value is integer hg/ha (1e4 scale) with heavy right skew (median 36,744; max 1,000,000) -> expect low linear/polynomial explanatory power; target scaling optional but coefficients ill-conditioned due to raw pesticide scale
no missing values in yield.csv / pesticides.csv; missing only in rainfall (774+6) and temp (2547)

modeling_plan_for_downstream.merge: inner join yield + pesticides + rainfall + temp on (country, year); aggregate temp by mean per (country, year); dropna before fit
modeling_plan_for_downstream.preprocessing: sklearn PolynomialFeatures(degree=2, include_bias=False) -> 9 columns (3 linear, 3 squares, 3 interactions)
modeling_plan_for_downstream.metric: r2_score(y, model.predict(X_poly)) on the fitted data, rounded to 4 decimals

sanity_reference_values_measured_in_this.comment: R2 is small in all variants: climate/pesticide levels explain only a few percent of cross-country yield variance. The duplicate-handling decision changes rows and R2; the recommended path is temp aggregated to one record per country-year (13,130 rows, R2 ~= 0.0301).
